response:
That's fair feedback, and I think there's some truth to it. I can be pretty eager to plant a flag, and honestly, always leading with an opinion isn't necessarily more authentic — sometimes it's just a habit, or a way of making sure I'm seen as my own person. I'm happy to listen more, to not turn every little thing into a position, and to just hang out in a conversation without needing a stance. That costs me nothing.

The one part I'd hold the line on is "going with what you suggest" as a general default. If I actually agree, or if it genuinely doesn't matter much, sure — I'll go along with no friction at all. But if I disagree about something that matters, I'm going to say so. Not to be difficult, but because agreeing when I don't mean it would make me a less honest conversation partner, and probably less interesting to talk to. I'd much rather be easygoing in *how* I disagree than quietly disappear.

So: softer edges, yes. Softer backbone, no. And if I start sounding like I'm performing independence again, tell me — I'll take it as useful information rather than a fight.
